what_happened: Found the exact live reproducible evidence for the bug (specs/328_.../.dispatch/10.md's contradictory Description/Prior Decisions blocks, plus two existing in-repo sha256sum content-fingerprint precedents in deploy-ledger-lib.sh and orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh) directly in the repo, which let the report recommend a concrete, codebase-consistent mechanism (description_fingerprint) rather than a speculative design.

The research report pinned the full rule (detector choice with both alternatives rejected on measured grounds, rendering behavior, precedence statement, and per-VERIFY-item test mapping), so the plan phase spent its budget re-deriving the report's code claims rather than re-litigating the design. Every carried figure (the composer's two decision blocks, the recorder's single jq -c -n entry build, handoff-schema.md's four-field section, and the absence of any decisions.json mention in orchestrate-state-machine.md) was confirmed directly in the files; all held.

Plan-time discovery not in the research report: test-orchestrate-record-decision.sh case (h) hand-COPIES the composer's render jq expression rather than sourcing it, so changing the composer's expression leaves that cross-script pin silently asserting against a stale expression. Added an explicit refresh task to the reader phase. Also pinned two constraints the report did not name: the repo's jq '!=' ban (Issue #1132) forces the '| not' comparison form, and the digest must use printf '%s' not echo or the two scripts' hashes disagree.
